title: Zelenskyy confirms Ukraine was behind attack on Russian warship off Libya
summary: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a naval base in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that sea drones sank the vessel in a surprise assault the…

blocks.text: Zelenskyy confirms Ukraine carried out drone attacks on Russian vessels off Libya

Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a naval base in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that sea drones sank the vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.

Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made sea drones in the operation, which struck the Russian corvette Merkury, according to Zelenskyy. The ship was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 invasion of its neighbour, the Ukrainian leader said in a post on X.
Zelenskyy described Sunday's attack as "exemplary" and said "the targets we set were achieved."
Russian officials made no immediate comment.

Within Ukraine, a Russian strike on a five-storey apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said Monday. A seven-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled from the rubble after the Sunday morning attack, rescue services said.
A rescue worker climbs a ladder to a balcony of a residential building damaged in a Russian strike in Kyiv on Monday. (Evgeniy Maloletka/The Associated Press)

Federico Borsari, a fellow with the Transatlantic Defence and Security Program at the Center for European Policy Analysis, told CBC News that while it isn't "completely novel" for Ukraine to deploy drones away from the main theatre of war — pointing to the skirmishes in the Black Sea — the Ukrainian attack off the North African coast demonstrates more than others before it that "there is no safe haven for Russian assets."

"I think the real key element here is that Ukraine has been able to deploy not just drones from ships or from secure locations near the areas where Russian assets are located, but also to deploy constant, near-real-time surveillance, reconnaissance, intelligence capabilities," he said.

David Hambling, a London, U.K.-based journalist and author who writes about war and military technology, said the attack carries wider implications for the use of drones in warfare. While the Houthis and Iranians have used unmanned sea vehicles for drone attacks in the Middle East, he said, the capabilities demonstrated by Ukraine in the near-five-year war with Russia are of a different magnitude.

If Ukraine can achieve this kind of attack, Hambling said, "that means the Iranians, the North Koreans, the Chinese, the Russians — anyone can potentially use the same technique to attack any ship anywhere and then deny responsibility."
Ukraine hails 'unique' attack
The operation — conducted near Benghazi, some 2,400 kilometres from the front line in Ukraine — was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces.

Ukraine has at times blindsided Russia during the war with ingenious attacks that embarrass Moscow, such as Operation Spiderweb in June last year, when drones launched from trucks hit more than 40 aircraft parked near airbases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometre front line snaking through southern and Eastern Ukraine, Kyiv's cutting-edge drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army.

In satellite images provided by Vantor, a vessel is seen at a naval base in Benghazi, Libya, before and after being struck. Ukraine claimed responsibility for the attack, saying it sank the Russian warship Merkury. (Vantor/CBC)

Ukraine has also hit Russian oil refineries as far away as western Siberia and other Russian warships in the Mediterranean, Zelenskyy noted in a live video address on Monday to a meeting of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.
"We keep finding ways to get back on our feet after every Russian attack," Zelenskyy said.
On Sunday, Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara near Benghazi, which Zelenskyy said Moscow used to transport weapons, and destroyed a Ka-27 military helicopter, he said.

Ukraine's Security Service, or SBU, described the operation as "unique." It said the cargo ship MV Angara was sanctioned and used to transport Russian military equipment, and the multipurpose Merkury regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including guarding the MV Angara.
The drones were delivered to a designated location and launched from a so-called "mothership" near the target, the SBU said.
A Ka-27 helicopter was on board the corvette and also went under, the SBU added.
Russian defences tried from air, sea and land to hit the attacking drones, it said.

blocks.text: Reuters verified the Angara and Merkury attack through satellite imagery and handout photos from the Libyan National Army, comparing the ships' superstructures, shapes and colours, as well as the position of nearby cranes.

The government in eastern Libya sent a letter to UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres and the UN Security Council, calling for an international investigation into the potential use of western Libya to prepare and launch Sunday's attack.
Several injured, Libyan officials say

Ukrainian forces are operating in western Libya under a covert deal endorsed by the West, and used the North African country's territory to strike a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in March, according to Libyan officials.

The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, were at the time operating mainly at an airbase in the coastal city of Misrata, but also in other military facilities in the capital Tripoli and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press earlier this year.
A Ukrainian drone approaches the Russian cargo ship MV Angara near Benghazi, Libya, in video provided by the Security Service of Ukraine on Monday. (Security Service of Ukraine/The Associated Press)

Libyan officials who were briefed on the attack told The Associated Press that at least four drones were intercepted while two hit the corvette, which is designed to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.
Residents in Benghazi heard loud explosions and saw flames at the base early Sunday. Civil defence units rushed to the site and extinguished the fire, authorities in eastern Libya said.

The vessel had docked to refuel and take on supplies as part of a co-operation agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, a statement said without providing details about the vessel or its cargo.
At least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded in the attack, one of the officials said.
The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.

Ambrey, a U.K.-based maritime security and risk intelligence firm, said that some of the explosions at the Benghazi Naval Base were likely caused by the detonation of ammunition on board the Russian warship.
